title: Makan Like a Local
description: Teh-O, bak chor mee, kueh and cendol — order the whole hawker menu by name.

items.note: Same 乌 as in 咖啡乌: no milk. Teh-O kosong has no sugar either.

example.zh: 老板， 一杯 茶乌 冰。
example.en: Boss, one iced teh-O.

items.note: The tea is "pulled" between two cups until it's frothy.

example.zh: 那 个 摊位 的 拉茶 最 好喝。
example.en: That stall's teh tarik is the best.

items.note: Iced Milo buried under a mountain of Milo powder.

example.zh: 我 要 一杯 美禄恐龙！
example.en: I want a Milo dinosaur!

example.zh: 玫瑰露加奶 是 粉红色 的。
example.en: Bandung is pink.

items.note: Named after mandarin ducks, which always come in pairs.

example.zh: 咖啡 加 茶， 就 是 鸳鸯。
example.en: Coffee plus tea is yuanyang.

example.zh: 天气 热， 喝 一杯 冰 豆花水。
example.en: It's hot — have a cold soya bean milk.

example.zh: 肉脞面 要 干 的 还是 汤 的？
example.en: Bak chor mee — dry or soup?

example.zh: 我 要 面薄， 多 辣椒。
example.en: Mee pok for me, extra chilli.

example.zh: 这 盘 福建炒虾面 很 香。
example.en: This plate of Hokkien mee smells amazing.

items.note: Pick your pieces — tofu, fishball, vegetables — and the stall cooks them for you.

example.zh: 酿豆腐 你 要 几 样？
example.en: How many pieces of yong tau foo do you want?

example.zh: 妈妈 早餐 喜欢 吃 米暹。
example.en: Mum likes mee siam for breakfast.

example.zh: 我们 去 吃 印度煎饼 当 宵夜。
example.en: Let's have roti prata for supper.

example.zh: 外婆 自己 包 薄饼。
example.en: Grandma wraps her own popiah.

example.zh: 下午 茶 吃 咖喱卜。
example.en: Curry puffs for afternoon tea.

items.note: Topped with 菜脯 (cài pú), fried preserved radish.

example.zh: 早餐 来 四个 水粿。
example.en: Four chwee kueh for breakfast.

example.zh: 猪肠粉 要 加 甜酱 吗？
example.en: Want sweet sauce on your chee cheong fun?

items.note: Tortoise-shaped for long life — given out at a baby's full-month celebration.

example.zh: 满月 要 送 红龟粿。
example.en: Ang ku kueh are given out at a baby's full month.

example.zh: 乌达 用 叶子 包 着 烤。
example.en: Otah is grilled wrapped in leaves.

example.zh: 浆绿 有 椰浆 和 黑糖。
example.en: Cendol has coconut milk and gula melaka.

example.zh: 清汤 可以 冷 吃 也 可以 热 吃。
example.en: Cheng tng can be eaten cold or hot.

example.zh: 文头雪 很 解渴。
example.en: Ice jelly really quenches your thirst.

items.note: Singapore writes it with 梿. And no, you can't bring one on the MRT.

example.zh: 地铁 上 不 可以 带 榴梿。
example.en: You can't bring durians on the MRT.

example.zh: 红毛丹 外面 有 很 多 毛。
example.en: Rambutans are very hairy on the outside.

items.note: Folk wisdom: eat it after durian to "cool" your body down.

example.zh: 吃 完 榴梿 要 吃 山竹。
example.en: Eat mangosteen after durian.

example.zh: 这个 参峇 很 辣。
example.en: This sambal is really spicy.

example.zh: 椰浆饭 有 江鱼仔 和 花生。
example.en: Nasi lemak comes with ikan bilis and peanuts.

example.zh: 亚喳 酸酸 甜甜 的。
example.en: Achar is sweet and sour.

example.zh: 过年 奶奶 会 煮 杂菜。
example.en: Grandma cooks chap chye at Chinese New Year.

example.zh: 三层肉 太 肥 了。
example.en: Pork belly is too fatty.

example.zh: 我 要 一 份 炒 高丽菜。
example.en: One portion of fried cabbage, please.

items.note: What you see on signs and in the news. 小贩中心 means the same thing.

example.zh: 熟食中心 星期一 关门 清洗。
example.en: The hawker centre closes on Monday for cleaning.

example.zh: 商场 楼上 有 一个 食阁。
example.en: There's a food court upstairs in the mall.

example.zh: 宵夜 只 有 快熟面。
example.en: There's only instant noodles for supper.

example.zh: 小孩 都 喜欢 吃 朱古力。
example.en: Kids all love chocolate.

items.note: Singaporeans say tāng chí; elsewhere it's often 勺子 (sháo zi).

example.zh: 老板， 可以 给 我 汤匙 吗？
example.en: Boss, can I have a spoon?

example.zh: 打包 要 塑胶袋 吗？
example.en: Need a plastic bag for the takeaway?
